src: APPSC AEE (Civil), AMVI, Agriculture Officer and Other Posts
s: Headquarters of United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) is located in
FAO is the abbreviation of
x: FAO stands for Food and Agriculture Organisation (headquartered in Rome); the other options are not real organisations.

s: The headquarters of IAAF is situated in
x: IAAF (now World Athletics) is headquartered in Monaco; the notes do not cover it.

s: The Headquarters of the ‘Greenpeace International’ is located at :
x: Greenpeace International is a non-governmental organization working in the field of environment. Its headquarters is located in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

s: Who is the Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund?
x: Kristalina Georgieva became Managing Director of the IMF on 1 October 2019, succeeding Christine Lagarde.

s: Who is the Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund? 14.
x: Kristalina Georgieva became Managing Director of the IMF on 1 October 2019, succeeding Christine Lagarde.

s: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)?
x: UNEP is headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya.

s: Where is the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) headquartered?
x: WMO, like WHO, ITU, WTO and ILO, is headquartered in Geneva.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: IAEA is headed by Rafael Grossi. Arsenio Dominguez is the Secretary-General of the IMO, headquartered in London.

s: Which is the oldest UN agency, established in 1865?
x: The ITU, founded in 1865, is the oldest UN agency; it has 194 members and is headquartered in Geneva, not London.

s: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus belongs to which country?
x: Tedros is Ethiopian. Celeste Saulo is Argentine, Arsenio Dominguez Panamanian and Qu Dongyu Chinese.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Gilbert F. Houngbo is from Togo, not Ghana. The other three institutional leadership-nationality pairs are correctly matched.

s: Which pair is correctly matched?
x: The IMF formally came into existence on 27 December 1945, while its operations began on 1 March 1947.

s: The 36-member Council is associated with which organisation?
x: ICAO, established in 1944 under the Chicago Convention, has a 36-member Council and is headquartered in Montreal.

s: Where is the UNFCCC Secretariat located?
x: The UNFCCC secretariat is in Bonn, with 198 Parties.

s: Where is the secretariat of the International Solar Alliance located?
x: The ISA secretariat is at Gurugram; New Delhi hosts CDRI.

s: In which year was the Bretton Woods Conference held?
x: The Bretton Woods Conference took place in 1944. Its ideas were associated with Harry Dexter White and John Maynard Keynes.

s: Khaled El-Enany, who became UNESCO Director-General in November 2025, belongs to which country?
x: El-Enany, an Egyptian Egyptologist, is UNESCO's first Arab head; he succeeded Audrey Azoulay of France.

s: Where was the 43rd UNESCO General Conference held, which elected Khaled El-Enany as Director-General?
x: He was elected on 6 November 2025 by the 43rd General Conference at Samarkand, Uzbekistan.

s: Gilbert F. Houngbo, Director-General of the ILO, belongs to which country?
x: The ILO head Houngbo is from Togo, not Ghana.

s: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Director-General of the WTO, belongs to which country?
x: The WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is Nigerian.

s: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva belongs to which country?
x: Georgieva is Bulgarian; Rebeca Grynspan (UNCTAD) is from Costa Rica and Grossi and Saulo are Argentine.

s: Which UN agency is headquartered in London?
x: IMO is in London; ITU and WMO are in Geneva and ICAO in Montreal.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UNESCO?
o: It has 194 members and 12 associate members.
Khaled El-Enany succeeded Audrey Azoulay as its head.
x: UNESCO's Executive Board has 58 members; the 36-member Council belongs to ICAO.

s: Where is the headquarters of INTERPOL?
x: INTERPOL is headquartered at Lyon, France.

s: Which two countries set up the UN Alliance of Civilizations in 2005?
x: The UN Alliance of Civilizations (New York) was set up in 2005 by Türkiye and Spain.

s: Who was the first African to become Director-General of the WHO, in 2017?
x: Tedros of Ethiopia became WHO DG in 2017, succeeding Margaret Chan, the first African to head the WHO.

s: Who is the President of the World Bank?
x: Ajay Banga, an Indian-born US national, is President of the World Bank.

s: Where is the headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)?
x: ICAO, created by the Chicago Convention (1944), is headquartered in Montreal.

s: The Bretton Woods Conference of 1944 was based on the ideas of which two economists?
o: Harry Dexter White and John Maynard Keynes
x: The Bretton Woods institutions grew from the plans of Harry Dexter White (US) and John Maynard Keynes (UK).

s: Who was Managing Director of the IMF from 2011 to 2019 and later became President of the European Central Bank?
x: Christine Lagarde headed the IMF in 2011-2019 and then became ECB President; Georgieva succeeded her.

s: When was the first meeting of the United Nations Security Council held on the threats artificial intelligence poses to international peace and stability
Which organisations are headed respectively by Rafael Grossi and Rebeca Grynspan, candidates for UN Secretary-General in 2026?
x: Rafael Grossi is Director General of the IAEA and Rebeca Grynspan is Secretary-General of UNCTAD.

s: The ITU Council accepted India's bid to host which event in 2030?
o: World Summit on the Information Society
x: The ITU Council accepted India's bid to host the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference 2030, known as PP-30.

s: India took over the chairmanship of the Kimberley Process on 1 January 2026 for which time?
x: India, a founding member, took over the chair on 1 January 2026 for the third time; the Process has 60 participants (59 countries and the EU).

s: Under Article 97 of the UN Charter, who appoints the UN Secretary-General?
o: The Economic and Social Council on the recommendation of the Security Council
The UN Security Council on the recommendation of the General Assembly
The International Court of Justice on the recommendation of the General Assembly
The UN General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council
x: Article 97 provides for appointment by the UN General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council.

s: Khalilur Rahman, elected President of the 81st UN General Assembly (2026-27), is from which country?
x: Khalilur Rahman of Bangladesh was elected in the Asia-Pacific Group's turn, defeating the candidate from Cyprus.

s: On which date does the five-year term of the next UN Secretary-General begin?
x: Guterres demits office at the end of 2026 and his successor's term begins on 1 January 2027.

s: Which term is India's election to the UN Human Rights Council for 2026-28?
x: India was elected unopposed to the UNHRC for 2026-28, its 7th term.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the U.S. exit from international bodies announced in January 2026?
o: It included the UNFCCC, IPCC and IRENA
The U.S. was described as the first country to attempt formal withdrawal from the UNFCCC
UN Women and UNFPA were among the bodies exited
The International Solar Alliance was not among the bodies exited
x: The ISA was among the bodies the U.S. exited, along with UNFPA, UN Women, UNHRC and UNCTAD.

s: When did the UN Security Council hold its first-ever meeting on the risks posed by artificial intelligence to international peace?
x: The first UNSC meeting on AI risks to peace was held in July 2023 (asked before). The other dates are distractors with no such first meeting.

s: UNMISS is the UN peacekeeping mission in which country?
x: UNMISS is in South Sudan; MONUSCO is in DR Congo, UNIFIL in Lebanon and MINURSO in Western Sahara.

s: Which UN peacekeeping mission is the referendum mission in Western Sahara?
x: MINURSO is the Western Sahara referendum mission; UNDOF is on the Golan Heights and UNFICYP in Cyprus.

s: Which UN peacekeeping mission ended after the host country withdrew consent in June 2023?
x: MINUSMA is no longer active because Mali withdrew consent in June 2023.

s: For which term was India re-elected to the UNESCO Executive Board in December 2025?
x: India was re-elected to the UNESCO Executive Board for 2025-29; 2025-28 is its ICAO Council term and 2026-28 its UNHRC term.

s: The Kimberley Process, chaired by India in 2026, has how many participants?
x: The Kimberley Process has 60 participants: 59 countries plus the EU.

s: A candidate for UN Secretary-General needs how many 'encourage' votes in the UNSC, with no P5 veto?
x: A candidate needs 9 'encourage' votes and no veto from a permanent member.

s:
Match the following UN peacekeeping missions with their host areas:
A. MONUSCO
B. UNDOF
C. UNFICYP
D. UNMISS
1. Cyprus
2. South Sudan
3. DR Congo
4. Golan Heights
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: MONUSCO is in DR Congo, UNDOF on the Golan Heights, UNFICYP in Cyprus and UNMISS in South Sudan.

s: Which of the following is not one of the UNESCO creative cities from India ?
x: The following Indian cities have been included in UNESCO’s Creative Cities Network: 1. Jaipur (2015) – in the field of Crafts and Folk Art 2. Varanasi (2015) – in the field of Music 3. Chennai (2017) – in the field of Music 4. Mumbai (2019) – in the field of Film 5. Hyderabad (2019) – in the field of Gastronomy 6. Srinagar (2021) – in the field of Crafts and Folk Art 7. Gwalior (2023) – in the field of Music 8. Kozhikode (2023) – in the field of Literature

s: In which country is the Angkorvat temple complex located?
x: Angkor Wat is in Cambodia (formerly Kampuchea), so option 4 is correct.

s: The brithplace of Christ is.
x: Jesus Christ is traditionally held to have been born in Bethlehem, not Jerusalem.

s:
With reference to Manipuri Sankirtana, consider the following statements.

I. It is a song and dance performance.

II. Cymbals are the only musical instruments used in the performance.

III. It is performed to narrate the life and deeds Lord Krishna.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Manipuri Sankirtana is a song-and-dance performance narrating the life and deeds of Lord Krishna, so I and III are correct. Statement II is wrong because it uses the pung (drum) along with cymbals, not cymbals alone.

s: Which of the following was included in 2016 by UNESCO in the list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
x: Yoga was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2016, while Vedic chanting and Ramlila were inscribed in 2008 and Sankirtana in 2013.

s: Which one of the following was the latest inclusion in the Intangible Cultural Heritage List of UNESCO? Indian Art and Culture PMF IAS IH – 239
x: Option (c) is correct: Garba is a traditional dance performed during the Hindu festival of Navaratri, which celebrates feminine energy, or 'Shakti'. It was included in the 2023 UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List. Option (a) is incorrect: Chhau dance, originating from eastern India, encompasses narratives from epics, folklore, and abstract themes, distinguished by styles from Seraikella, Purulia, and Mayurbhanj. It was included in the list in 2010. Option (b) is incorrect: Durga Puja is an annual festival celebrated primarily in Kolkata and other parts of India, dedicated to the worship of the goddess Durga over ten days in September or October. It was included in the list in 2021. Option (d) is incorrect: Kumbh Mela was included in 2017.

s: Deepavali was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in December 2025 as India's which element?
x: Deepavali became India's 16th ICH element on 10 December 2025; 45 is Sarnath's World Heritage number.

s: Where was the 20th session of UNESCO's Intergovernmental Committee on Intangible Heritage (December 2025) held?
x: The 20th session met at the Red Fort, New Delhi (8-13 December 2025), the first time India hosted it.

s: Which Indian city joined the UNESCO Creative Cities Network for Gastronomy in 2025?
x: Lucknow joined in 2025 as India's second Gastronomy city; Hyderabad was the first, in 2019.

s: Which of the following pairs (UNESCO Creative City – field) is correctly matched?
x: Kozhikode is a City of Literature (2023). Gwalior is Music, Mumbai Film and Srinagar Crafts and Folk Arts.

s: Where is the Exploration Museum with an Astronaut Monument honouring Apollo astronauts?
x: The Exploration Museum at Húsavík, Iceland, tells the history of exploration; its Astronaut Monument (2015) honours 32 Apollo astronauts.

s: In which country is the Makli necropolis, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, located?
x: Makli necropolis, near Thatta in Sindh, Pakistan, is one of the world's largest and a World Heritage Site since 1981.

s: Which country was certified as Malaria-free by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2024?
x: Cabo Verde was certified malaria-free by WHO in 2024; the other options were not certified that year.

s: At which meeting was the Global Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance for 2026–2036 adopted?
x: The 79th World Health Assembly, held in May 2026, adopted the Global Action Plan on AMR 2026–2036.

s: In the WHO Pandemic Agreement negotiations, India backs which grouping?
x: India backs the developing-country Group for Equity in the negotiations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Fiji — 26th country to eliminate trachoma, October 2025
x: India was certified polio-free in 2014, not malaria-free. Cabo Verde, Fiji and Sri Lanka are correctly matched with the stated certifications.

s: Which country was the first in the Americas to eliminate leprosy?
x: WHO certified Chile as the first country in the Americas to eliminate leprosy.

s: In which year was India certified polio-free?
x: India was certified polio-free in 2014; 2016 is Sri Lanka's malaria-free year.

s: On which date was the WHO Pandemic Agreement adopted?
x: The Agreement was adopted on 20 May 2025; talks on its PABS annex resumed in Geneva in July 2026.

s: In October 2025, Fiji became the 26th country to eliminate which disease?
x: Fiji was certified the 26th country to eliminate trachoma, its first NTD eliminated.

s: Which country became the first in Africa to end onchocerciasis (river blindness)?
x: Niger became the first in Africa and fifth in the world to end onchocerciasis, in late 2025.

s: Which country was most recently certified malaria-free by WHO, in July 2025?
x: Timor-Leste was certified malaria-free in July 2025; Cabo Verde in 2024 and Sri Lanka in 2016.

s: In which countries is wild poliovirus now endemic?
x: Wild poliovirus is endemic only in Pakistan and Afghanistan; India was certified polio-free in 2014.

s: What does the still-unfinished annex of the WHO Pandemic Agreement deal with?
x: The PABS (Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing) annex is unfinished; talks resumed in Geneva in July 2026.

s: Which country became the first in the WHO South-East Asia Region to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies?
x: Bhutan became the first in the WHO South-East Asia Region to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies (September 2026).

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
s: Union Civil Aviation Minister K. Rammohan Naidu was selected for which prestigious recognition?

Match
List I with
List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists:
List I (INTERPOL Notice)
List II (Description)
A. Silver Notice
1. To seek information on unidentified bodies
B. Blue Notice
2. To collect additional information about a person
C. Black Notice
3. To provide warning about criminal activities
D. Green Notice
4. To identify and trace criminal assets
Code:
x: Option (c) is correct: Silver Notice: To identify and trace criminal assets. • Blue Notice: To collect additional information about a person's identity, location, or activities in relation to a criminal investigation. • Black Notice: To seek information on unidentified bodies. • Green Notice: To provide a warning about a person's criminal activities where the person is considered to be a possible threat to public safety. International Relations PMF IAS Misc – 38

s: INTERPOL stands for
x: INTERPOL stands for International Police Organisation (International Criminal Police Organization), headquartered in Lyon.

s: Which organisations jointly sponsor the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)?
x: The IPCC is sponsored by UNEP and WMO. Its AR6 synthesis report was released on 20 March 2023, and its AR7 cycle began in July 2023.

s: Which organisation sponsors the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, known as the “Seed Treaty”?
x: The ITPGRFA is sponsored by FAO and concerns plant genetic resources in harmony with the Convention on Biological Diversity.

s: The ‘Great Reset’ is an initiative of which organisation?
x: The Great Reset was a World Economic Forum initiative launched in 2020.

s: Which of the following INTERPOL notices is correctly matched with its purpose?
o: Blue Notice – Locate and arrest a wanted person pending extradition
Silver Notice – Information on a person's identity, location or activities
x: The Yellow Notice is for missing persons. Red is to locate and arrest pending extradition, Blue seeks information on identity/location, and Silver (2025) traces criminal assets.

s:
Which of the following international roles are associated with India in 2026?
1. Chair of the Kimberley Process
2. Host of ITU PP-30
3. Founder of ISA, CDRI and GBA
x: India chairs the Kimberley Process in 2026, is to host ITU PP-30 and is a founder of the ISA, CDRI and GBA.

s: What is the Colombo Process?
o: A regional forum of Asian labour-sending countries on overseas employment
An INTERPOL system for tracing criminal assets
A WEF initiative on global economic restructuring
A UN mechanism for electing non-permanent members
x: The Colombo Process is a regional forum of Asian labour-sending countries concerned with overseas employment.

s: Which country is the sixth member of the Colombo Security Conclave, formed in 2020?
x: The Conclave comprises India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh and Seychelles, with Seychelles as the 6th member. Bangladesh is a member but not the sixth; Myanmar and Indonesia are not members.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kimberley Process — conflict-diamond certification — no headquarters
Global Biofuels Alliance — India's G20 — biofuels
x: CDRI was sponsored by India in 2019 and is headquartered in New Delhi. Japan and Tokyo are not its sponsor and secretariat combination.

s: Where is the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) headquartered?
x: CDRI, launched by India in 2019, is headquartered in New Delhi, not Tokyo; Gurugram hosts the ISA.

s: What does the U.S.-led 'Pax Silica', which India joined in February 2026, concern?
o: Maritime security in the Indian Ocean
Critical minerals, semiconductor and AI supply chains
x: Pax Silica covers critical minerals, semiconductor and AI supply chains; energy resilience is the aim of Japan's POWERR Asia.

s: POWERR Asia, launched under AZEC Plus in April 2026, is an initiative of which country?
x: POWERR Asia is Japan's initiative under AZEC Plus for energy resilience; India is a participant.

s: In India, which agency serves as the INTERPOL National Central Bureau?
x: The CBI is India's INTERPOL National Central Bureau and seeks Red Notices.

s: Which INTERPOL notice, the newest one introduced in 2025, is used to identify and trace criminal assets?
x: The Silver Notice (2025) is the newest INTERPOL notice and is used to trace criminal assets.

s:
Which among the following countries got membership into BRICS bloc with effect from 1st January, 2024?

I. Egypt

II. Argentina

III. Indonesia

IV. Ethiopia

V. Saudi Arabia
x: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and UAE joined BRICS on 1 Jan 2024. Argentina declined its invitation and Indonesia joined only in 2025. Saudi Arabia was invited and was counted by the question as a member, so option 4 (I, IV, V) is the answer key's choice.

s: Which of the following is the newest member of the Eurozone?
x: Croatia, which joined on 1 January 2023, was the newest Eurozone member among the options as of the exam year; Bulgaria joined only in 2026.

s: Which of the following countries is not a member of SCO ?
x: India was only an SCO observer in 2013 and became a full member in 2017, while China, Russia and Uzbekistan were already members.

s: Which of the following countries was readmitted to the Common Wealth recently?
x: Pakistan's Commonwealth suspension was lifted and it was readmitted in May 2008.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: New Development Bank — Chair in 2026: Uzbekistan
x: Bangladesh is the BIMSTEC chair for 2026. The other pairings incorrectly assign leadership roles not stated for those organisations.

s: Which of the following countries joined BRICS from 1 January 2024?
o: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates
Argentina, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia and Egypt
Ethiopia, Saudi Arabia, Indonesia and the United Arab Emirates
x: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates joined BRICS from 1 January 2024. Argentina declined the invitation, while Indonesia joined in 2025 and Saudi Arabia's status remained unconfirmed.

s: Where is the Secretariat of APEC located?
x: APEC has 21 economies and its Secretariat is in Singapore; India is only an observer.

s: Which country was invited to join BRICS at Johannesburg in August 2023 but declined?
x: Argentina declined; Egypt and Ethiopia joined on 1 January 2024 and Indonesia in January 2025.

s: Which country became NATO's 32nd member in 2024?
x: Sweden joined as the 32nd member in 2024; Finland had joined as the 31st in 2023.

s: Which country became the 10th member of the New Development Bank and its first from Central Asia?
x: Uzbekistan became the NDB's 10th member and the first from Central Asia; the NDB is headquartered in Shanghai.

s: Which country joined the New Development Bank (NDB) in 2023?
x: Egypt joined the NDB (set up by the 2014 Fortaleza Declaration, HQ Shanghai) in 2023. Uzbekistan later became the 10th member and first from Central Asia. Argentina and Indonesia are BRICS-expansion names, not NDB entrants.

s: Which of the following is a Maastricht criterion for entry into the Eurozone?
x: Eurozone entry criteria include a fiscal deficit below 3% of GDP, debt below 60% of GDP and participation in ERM II.

s: Which country became the 21st member of the Eurozone?
x: Bulgaria became the Eurozone's 21st member.

s: What is India's status in APEC?
x: APEC has 21 economies and its Secretariat in Singapore; India is not a member, only an observer.

s: In which year did the African Union become a member of the G20?
x: The G20 has 19 countries, the EU and the African Union, which joined in 2023.

s: Which country joined BRICS in January 2025?
x: Indonesia joined in January 2025. Egypt joined in 2024, Argentina declined and Saudi Arabia has not formally joined.

s: Which country became the 119th member of the International Solar Alliance?
x: Malta became the 119th member of the ISA.

s: Where was the APEC summit of 2025 held?
x: The 2025 APEC summit was held at Gyeongju, South Korea, where China proposed WAICO.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Hague Conventions (HCCH) – UK–EU post-Brexit trade rules for Northern Ireland
x: The Stockholm Convention (2001) covers persistent organic pollutants. Chicago is civil aviation, HCCH is private international law and the Windsor Framework covers Northern Ireland trade rules.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Basel Convention — prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals
x: The Vienna Convention of 1985 concerns protection of the ozone layer. Rotterdam concerns prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals, Basel concerns transboundary hazardous waste, and the Windsor Framework concerns post-Brexit UK–EU trade rules for Northern Ireland.

s: Which convention governs the transboundary movement of hazardous waste?
x: The Basel Convention of 1989 governs transboundary hazardous waste. It also includes a plastic-waste amendment and stronger rules relating to e-waste.

s: In which year was the Basel Convention adopted?
x: The Basel Convention dates from 1989, after the Chicago Convention (1944) and before Stockholm (2001) and Minamata (2013).

s: On which date did the BBNJ (High Seas) Treaty enter into force?
x: Adopted in March 2023, the BBNJ Treaty entered into force on 17 January 2026; India has signed but not ratified it.

s: What does the Minamata Convention (2013) deal with?
x: The Minamata Convention concerns mercury, with dental amalgam to be phased out by 2034; POPs belong to the Stockholm Convention.

s: Which country became the first South Asian party to the UN Water Convention (Helsinki, 1992)?
x: Bangladesh became the first South Asian party to the Water Convention, which governs transboundary rivers and lakes.

s:
With reference to the five UN outer-space treaties, consider the following:
1. India has ratified the Moon Agreement of 1979.
2. India has signed all five treaties.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: India has signed all five and ratified four; the exception is the 1979 Moon Agreement, which India has not ratified.

s: In whose name are treaties concluded in India?
x: Treaties concluded by India are concluded in the name of the President. Article 253 empowers Parliament to legislate for their implementation.

s: What does Article 253 of the Constitution of India enable Parliament to do?
o: appoint the secretariat of every UN convention
ratify every treaty without executive action
withdraw India from any treaty without consultation
legislate for implementing treaties and international agreements
x: Article 253 empowers Parliament to make laws for implementing treaties, agreements and conventions with foreign countries or decisions made at international conferences.

s: India's refusal to join which of the following has been defended as protecting its policy space?
o: The IFD initiative and the WHO Pandemic Agreement
The UN Cybercrime Convention and the WHO Pandemic Agreement
The IFD initiative and the UN Cybercrime Convention
x: India's refusals on Investment Facilitation for Development and the Cybercrime Convention are defended as protecting policy space; the Pandemic Agreement is a separate matter.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the UN Convention against Cybercrime?
o: It is the first global cybercrime treaty, adopted in December 2024
It becomes binding 90 days after 40 ratifications
It was opened for signature at Hanoi in October 2025
x: The Convention's secretariat is UNODC, not UNCTAD.

s: Under the Kigali Amendment, beyond which date will India stop clearances for new HFC production?
x: India will stop clearances for new hydrofluorocarbon production beyond 31 December 2027 under the Kigali Amendment.

s: When did a joint Congress at Versailles approve France's constitutional guarantee of abortion freedom?
x: The joint Congress at Versailles approved it on 4 March 2024 (780-72).

s: What does the Windsor Framework (2023) concern?
o: UK-EU post-Brexit trade rules for Northern Ireland
x: The Windsor Framework sets UK-EU post-Brexit trade rules for Northern Ireland.

s: Which instrument on ozone-depleting substances has been universally ratified by 197 parties?
x: The Montreal Protocol (1987) is universally ratified (197); Stockholm covers POPs, Rotterdam prior informed consent and Basel hazardous waste.

s: What does the Rotterdam Convention deal with?
o: Prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals
x: Rotterdam = prior informed consent; Stockholm = POPs; Minamata = mercury; Vienna/Montreal = ozone.

s: The Apostille Convention (1961) is one of the conventions of which body?
o: Hague Conference on Private International Law
x: The Hague Conventions (HCCH) cover private international law, including the Apostille (1961) and Child Abduction (1980) conventions.

s: What is India's status on the BBNJ (High Seas) Treaty?
x: India has signed but not ratified the BBNJ Treaty, which entered into force on 17 January 2026.

s: Which was the first country to explicitly guarantee the freedom to have an abortion in its Constitution?
x: France did so through a joint Congress at Versailles on 4 March 2024 (vote 780-72).

s: Between which two countries were the US-brokered Washington Accords signed on 4 December 2025?
x: The Washington Accords of 4 December 2025 were a US-brokered peace deal between the DRC and Rwanda.

s: Under whose chairmanship did the European Convention draft the EU Constitution, which failed in the 2005 referendums?
x: The European Convention under Valery Giscard d'Estaing drafted the EU Constitution; after it failed in 2005, the Lisbon Treaty (2009) replaced it.

s: By which year does the Minamata Convention require dental amalgam to be phased out?
x: The Minamata Convention (2013) on mercury provides for phasing out dental amalgam by 2034.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about criticisms of the WTO and the Bretton Woods institutions?
o: The WTO Appellate Body is paralysed.
India is blocking the Investment Facilitation for Development (IFD) agreement.
A voting imbalance continues in the Bretton Woods institutions.
The Bretton Woods institutions have abolished quota-based voting.
x: Quota-based voting has not been abolished; the criticism is a continuing voting imbalance. Appellate Body paralysis and India's blocking of IFD are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about the India-Oman CEPA:
1. It provides duty-free treatment for 99% of India's exports.
2. It is India's first CEPA with a GCC country.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The India-Oman CEPA (signed December 2025, in force June 2026) makes 99% of India's exports duty-free; it is India's second GCC CEPA, not the first.

s: The WTO e-commerce moratorium lapsed in March 2026 after the failure of which Ministerial Conference?
x: The failure of MC14 and the lapse of the e-commerce moratorium were reported in March 2026.

s: In which years was the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) signed and brought into force respectively?
x: GATT was signed in 1947 and entered into force in 1948.

s: Which trade agreement has been described as the 'Mother of All Deals'?
x: The India-EU FTA is called the 'Mother of All Deals'; the India-UK CETA is the 'Gold standard' deal.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: India signed the CEPA with the UAE in 2022. ECTA was with Australia, TEPA with EFTA and CETA with the UK.

s: Which WTO subsidy box covers trade-distorting domestic support that is subject to a cap based on de minimis limits?
x: Amber Box subsidies are trade-distorting domestic support measures and are subject to prescribed limits, including de minimis ceilings.

s: Support tied to production-limiting programmes is classified under which WTO subsidy box?
